title: wsutil:wslog: Introduce fatal log count
description:
When using the fatal log option, allow for more than one fatal log
item to appear before trapping the program.

AI-Assisted: no

changes_data.diff:
@@ -8,6 +8,8 @@ Levels are case insensitive.
 --log-fatal <level>:: Abort the program if any messages are logged at the specified level or higher.
 For example, "warning" aborts on any "warning", "critical", or "error" messages.
 
+--log-fatal-count <count>:: The amount of fatal log messages which may pass before the program is aborted.
+
 // XXX List available domains if no list is provided?
 --log-domains <list>:: Only print messages for the specified log domains, e.g. "GUI,Epan,sshdump".
 List of domains must be comma-separated. Can be negated with "!" as the first character (inverts the match).

@@ -437,9 +437,12 @@ Sometimes it can be helpful to abort the program right after a log message of a
 
 The following environment variables are used to configure a trap by the logging system:
 
-WIRESHARK_LOG_FATAL, or --log_fatal::
+WIRESHARK_LOG_FATAL, or --log-fatal::
 This is the level for which log messages are fatal. This can either be "critical" or "warning" level.
 
+WIRESHARK_LOG_FATAL_COUNT, or --log-fatal-count::
+This is the amount of fatal log messages which may pass before the program is trapped.
+
 WIRESHARK_LOG_FATAL_DOMAIN, WIRESHARK_LOG_FATAL_DOMAINS, or --log-fatal-domain, --log-fatal-domains::
 These are the domain(s) where output of a log message is fatal. This is less commonly used than the fatal log level setting above.

@@ -283,6 +283,30 @@ WS_DLL_PUBLIC
 enum ws_log_level ws_log_set_fatal_level_str(const char *str_level);
 
 
+/**
+ * @brief Set the fatal log count.
+ *
+ * Sets the fatal log count at which calls to ws_log() of the configured level
+ * will abort the program. Must be 1 or higher.
+ *
+ * @param count  Fatal log count before program is trapped.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void ws_log_set_fatal_count(uint32_t count);
+
+
+/**
+ * @brief Set the fatal log count from a string.
+ *
+ * Same as ws_log_set_fatal_count(), but accepts the count as a string.
+ *
+ * @param str_count  String representation of the fatal log count.
+ * @return           true if the string was a valid count, false otherwise.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+bool ws_log_set_fatal_count_str(const char *str_count);
+
+
 /**
  * @brief Set the active log writer.
  *

 /** Logging options for command line
 */

     {"log-domains",           ws_required_argument, NULL, LONGOPT_WSLOG_LOG_DOMAIN}, \
